title: Movie Studios Give Away Cash to Promote Films
summary:
How do you get people excited about a new movie? Two movie studios tried a simple idea: give away money.

The film "How to Rob a Bank" opens in North American theaters on November 13. To promote it, a special ATM was placed in movie theaters around Los Angeles for four days. Fans who followed clues on social media could find the machine and a secret PIN — and the machine would pay out a single $100 bill.

Another film, "Ebenezer," opens the same day. It is about Ebenezer Scrooge, the famous character who hates spending money. The studio set up a Venmo account for Scrooge. People asked the account for money — but the only payments it sent were single cents!

One fan even sent the account about $30. A few days later, she got all her money back, plus an extra penny and an invitation to a special screening in New York.
why_it_matters: Next time you see a company giving away money online, you will know it is an advertising trick — and to be careful before sending money back.
